So perhaps the NON_RETRYABLE_CODES in the current code doesn't include "PAYMENT_DECLINED", which is why those errors are being retried. But the user's problem is that even when retryable is false, the code retries. So the should_retry function needs to check both the retryable flag and the error code.

So modifying the should_retry function: if retryable is False, then return False. Also, if the error_code is in NON_RETRYABLE_CODES, return False. Otherwise, check if the attempt is less than MAX_RETRIES.

def should_retry(error_code, retryable, attempt):

That way, if either retryable is False or the error code is non-retryable, we don't retry. That would prevent retries for those cases, leading to only one attempt (the initial call) for non-retryable errors.
